title: Solid-state electronics knowledge check
summary: Check the distinctions that keep component selection honest: references, bias, drive, ratings, heat and stored energy.

blocks.title: Explain the boundary, not just the answer
blocks.body: Work each question without a datasheet first. Then use the explanation to identify which lesson or specification you need to revisit. Answers reset when the page closes.

blocks.heading: 1. Doping
blocks.prompt: Which statement about n-type silicon is correct?
options: It is permanently negatively charged.
Electrons are majority carriers, while the material remains electrically neutral overall.
It is an insulator until reverse breakdown.
blocks.explanation: Donor doping increases the population of mobile electrons without turning the entire material into a charged object.

blocks.heading: 2. Diode forward voltage
blocks.prompt: Why is “a silicon diode drops 0.7 V” incomplete?
options: Forward voltage depends on current, temperature and device construction.
Every diode actually drops exactly 1 V.
Forward voltage applies only in reverse bias.
blocks.explanation: A datasheet states or plots forward voltage under specific conditions; 0.7 V is only a rough model for some junction diodes.

blocks.heading: 3. BJT switching
blocks.prompt: What best establishes base drive for a saturated BJT switch?
options: Maximum listed current gain.
A conservative forced gain plus verification of drive current and VCE(sat) conditions.
The collector-emitter voltage rating alone.
blocks.explanation: Switching design should not depend on a typical or maximum active-region gain.

blocks.heading: 4. MOSFET enhancement
options: The gate voltage that guarantees minimum RDS(on).
The test-defined point where channel conduction begins at a small stated current.
The maximum safe drain voltage.
blocks.explanation: Use RDS(on) specified at the actual gate drive, not threshold, to judge low-resistance enhancement.

blocks.heading: 5. Conduction loss
blocks.prompt: If MOSFET current doubles while on-resistance stays constant, what happens to I²R conduction loss?
options: It stays the same.
It doubles.
It becomes four times larger.
blocks.explanation: Squaring twice the current gives four times the loss. Real RDS(on) can also rise with temperature.

blocks.heading: 6. Inductive turn-off
blocks.prompt: What must a switching design do with energy stored in a coil?
options: Provide a rated path or clamp that removes the energy safely.
Assume it disappears when the control signal falls.
Send it through the controller logic pin.
blocks.explanation: Inductor current cannot change instantly. The turn-off path determines voltage stress and current decay.

blocks.heading: 7. Absolute maximum
blocks.prompt: How should an absolute-maximum rating be used?
options: As a recommended continuous operating point.
As a boundary not to exceed, with normal operation designed inside it.
As a typical value that may be ignored.
blocks.explanation: Absolute maximum ratings are damage boundaries, not promised performance points.

blocks.heading: 8. Turn results into a review plan

items.label: Name each miss
items.detail: Write the topic, not only the question number.

items.label: Locate the source
items.detail: Find the lesson block or manufacturer document that answers it.

items.label: Explain it aloud
items.detail: Use control path, load path, reference and energy-flow language.
